summary: Piotr Balcerowicz works in Indology and philosophy. Educated at Warsaw, Banaras Hindu University, Hamburg, and the Polish Academy of Sciences, he served as Professor of Indology at the University of Warsaw (2011) and Professor of International Relations at SWPS University (2008–2011).

Piotr Klafkowski is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań under Jerzy Bańczerowski. He also studied under traditional teachers Lobsang Jamspal, Geleg Gyatsho, Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche, and Nyalo Tulku Jampa Kelsang Rinpoche.

Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and later taught Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche and Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche.

Poerbatjaraka was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate from Leiden University under Nicolaas Johannes Krom. He founded Udayana University and was a professor at Gadjah Mada University (~1950–1964), the University of Indonesia (~1950–1964), and Udayana (~1958–1964).

Polly Young-Eisendrath is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Ohio University, Goddard College, and Washington University in St. Louis, underwent Zen training under Philip Kapleau, and became clinical associate professor of psychiatry at the University of Vermont in 1994.
Pori Park specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and has served as an assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.
Poulami Ray is an archaeology and history researcher who studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen. She held an appointment as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held posts at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture and as a professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 2009).
Prabhasa Dharma was an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies. She received traditional training under Zen masters Kyozan Joshu Sasaki starting in 1967 and Seikaku Hirata.

Prabodh Chandra Bagchi worked in Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, earning a State Doctorate at the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at the University of Calcutta (1930–1944, 1949–1951), Peking University (1947), and Visva-Bharati University (1945, 1954–1956).

Prafulla Chandra Ray was an Indology and history scholar educated at Vidyasagar College, Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Edinburgh. He held posts at Presidency University (1911–1916) and the University of Calcutta (Palit Professor of Chemistry, 1936).
Pragati Sahni specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Damien Keown and has served as an associate professor at the University of Delhi (attested 2026).
Praggnaparamita Biswas is an Indologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Ratna Basu. She has held an appointment as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Prahlad Pradhan was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Patna University and Visva-Bharati University. His posts included research fellow at Visva-Bharati (~1939–1944), professor at Utkal University (~1960–1975), and principal at Gangadhar Meher University.

Pramod Chandra was an art historian in South Asian archaeology and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Mumbai. He served as professor at the University of Chicago (1971–1980) and Bickford Professor at Harvard University (1980–2004).
Prasarn Lao-areun specializes in philosophy and Indology. He studied under Viroj Inthanon and completed his PhD at the University of Mysore (attested 2014).

Pratap Chandra Chunder was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University (~1936–1940) and the University of Calcutta (~1938–1947), where he was taught by Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.

Pratapaditya Pal is a curator and art historian in Indology, Tibetology, and archaeology with PhDs from Calcutta and Cambridge. He held curatorial posts at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, LACMA, and the Art Institute of Chicago, and edited Marg.

id: P:Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
summary: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark was a researcher in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Lycée Janson-de-Sailly and the London School of Economics (~1935–1951), and served in the Office of Strategic Services (~1943–1945).

Priyanku Chakraborty works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Supervised for doctoral studies by Aishwarya Biswas, Chakraborty holds the post of Rajendralal Mitra Research Fellow in Buddhist Studies at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
